title: apricity-score: effective grid in Clip::from_json, validation, explain line
description:
## Intent
The compiler warps with the effective grid.

## Scope
- `crates/apricity-score/src/manifest.rs`: `Marker` gains `beat: Option<f64>` and `source`; `Clip::from_json` validates your warp markers (order, count, range; errors `file: annotations.markers[i]: …`) and, with two or more, replaces `rhythm.warp_markers` and records `grid: Grid::Yours(n) | Grid::Analysis`.
- `rhythm.beats` stays the analysis's (per-beat loudness and chroma are indexed by it and are time-based through `beat_indices`); document that in a comment.
- `Timeline::explain` prints `grid: yours (N warp markers)` or `grid: analysis`.
- `apricity-daw::WarpMap::from_clip` uses the effective grid (makes the M4 export scenario green).

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-score -p apricity-daw -p apricity-cli` (compile, explain and export scenarios green).

Commit: `feat(<this id>): compile with warp markers of yours`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
